subject: Energy
title: Energy Density
description: A fast breakdown of Energy Density for builders.

hook.text: Energy density measures how much energy is packed per kilogram of fuel—and the differences are enormous.

buildup.text: Gasoline holds about 46 MJ/kg. A lithium-ion battery holds about 0.9 MJ/kg—roughly 50 times less.

discovery.text: That's why electric cars need heavy battery packs—their fuel stores far less energy per kilogram than gasoline.

twist.text: Hydrogen has the highest energy density by mass at 142 MJ/kg—but it's a gas, so per liter it's very low.

climax.text: Uranium has 80 trillion joules per kilogram—about 2 million times more energy-dense than gasoline.

punchline.text: Same weight, vastly different punch—that's energy density.

quiz.question: Which fuel has the highest energy density by mass?
